title: Gift Cards vs Vouchers vs Cash: Which Diwali Gift Keeps Its Value?
excerpt: A voucher can beat cash by Rs 4,680 on a Rs 15,000 employer gift in 2026, but cards expire in as little as 12 months and cannot be turned back into money. Here is the full comparison.
body:
• For employer Diwali gifts in 2026, non-cash vouchers and gift cards are tax-free below Rs 15,000 per employee for the whole tax year under Rule 15 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026; cash is taxable from the first rupee.
  • The tax gap is concrete: Rs 15,000 given as a voucher stays Rs 15,000, while Rs 15,000 as a cash bonus leaves about Rs 10,320 for an employee in the 30% slab.
  • Gift cards carry clocks and locks: Amazon Pay e-gift cards expire 12 months from delivery, cannot be transferred to a bank account, cannot be cancelled, and the balance cannot be combined with UPI or cards at checkout.
  • Brand vouchers bought at a discount (typically 1%-8% off face value) are restricted to one retailer and often valid only 6-12 months.

Diwali falls on November 8 this year, and the choice between a gift card, a voucher and cash is not just about presentation. The three are taxed differently, expire differently and lose value in different ways. The rules below decide what the recipient keeps.

Cash: flexible, but taxed first

Cash has no expiry date, no retailer lock-in and no fees. Its weakness is tax. According to TaxGST's Diwali corporate gifting guide, cash gifts, bank transfers and gift allowances paid through salary never qualify for the employer gift exemption and are taxable from the first rupee, exactly like salary. A Diwali bonus is added to payroll and taxed at the employee's slab rate. Gifts from non-relatives outside employment are tax-free only up to Rs 50,000 in aggregate per year; above that, the full amount is taxable as income from other sources.

Gift cards and vouchers: tax-free window, with fine print

Non-cash gifts, vouchers and tokens from an employer are valued at nil for tax if the aggregate for the tax year stays below Rs 15,000 per employee, under Rule 15 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026, notified on March 20, 2026 and effective from tax year 2026-27. The old limit was Rs 5,000. Two details matter: the limit is annual and aggregate, so a Rs 7,000 Diwali voucher plus a Rs 5,500 anniversary gift plus a Rs 3,000 birthday card totals Rs 15,500 and breaches it; and breaching works as a cliff, with the entire amount becoming a taxable perquisite, not just the excess.

The fine print sits on the card itself. Amazon's own gift card terms, read in full by Zoutons in its October 2026 rules summary, show the pattern for prepaid cards in India: an e-gift card expires 12 months from the date of delivery (15 months for scheduled-email cards), a single card runs from Rs 10 to Rs 10,000, the balance cannot be transferred to a bank account, a purchased card cannot be cancelled or returned, and a gift card balance cannot be combined with UPI, credit or debit cards, net banking or EMI on an order, so the balance must cover an order on its own or wait. Voucher platforms such as GyFTR list most Diwali brand cards as valid for 6-12 months, in denominations commonly from Rs 500 to Rs 10,000, sold at discounts of about 1%-8% depending on the brand: the giver pays less than the recipient spends.

Which one wins, by situation

For an employer, the voucher wins inside the limit: TaxGST's worked comparison shows an employee in the 30% slab keeping the full Rs 15,000 as a voucher against about Rs 10,320 as a taxed cash bonus, a Rs 4,680 difference created only by the instrument. Employers should still budget the full invoice cost, because GST input tax credit is blocked on gifted goods under Section 17(5)(h) of the CGST Act: a Rs 10,000 hamper with 18% GST costs Rs 11,800. Gifts stay outside GST supply treatment up to Rs 50,000 per employee per year.

For personal gifting, cash wins when the recipient may not shop at one retailer or may sit on the gift past a 12-month expiry. A discounted brand voucher wins when you know the store: buying at 5%-8% below face value is a saving cash cannot match. A general-purpose gift card sits between the two, but check the delivery date, because the expiry clock starts on delivery, not when the recipient adds the card. Keep the 16-digit reference ID on Amazon Pay cards; support asks for it if a balance expires.

The diaspora angle

For NRIs gifting family in India, eligibility matters more than the discount. Amazon states that international customers are not eligible to use its Indian gift cards and cards bought on other marketplaces cannot be added to an Indian account, so buy on the Indian storefront and pick a denomination the recipient can spend in one order, since balances do not combine with other payment methods.
